residuals.name: a merge state that differs by its viewer
residuals.check: stand-ins: a behaviour a stand-in declares not modelled
residuals.at: gh-threads\.ts:\d+ Not modelled: a merge state that differs by its viewer, where the world answers one merge state to every viewer
residuals.words: The world answers one merge state to every viewer. Production gave the review App `BLOCKED` and the implement App `CLEAN` on cybermonklabs/legion#4461 (reads of 12:55Z to 13:00Z on 2026-11-19, head `21dc91c7`, carrying three review App commits); the pull request then merged through the queue at 14:02:33Z as `73e417f113`. GitHub's rule behind the per-viewer answer is not known, so it is not modelled. Reviewers and the implementer can see different states in production only where a reviewer reads the merge state after its own approval. A batch that loses a run to it is what pays for a model.
residuals.source: packages/pi-envoy/scripts/README.md, "Which of the world's answers are pinned, and to what"; gh-threads.ts's `mergeStateOf`

residuals.name: the wrapper's refusal of a write whose repository GitHub answers 404
residuals.check: stand-ins: a behaviour a stand-in declares not modelled
residuals.at: gh-standin\.ts:\d+ The wrapper's refusal of a write whose repository GitHub answers 404 .* is not modelled: a write naming another repository of the world's owner passes the owner refusal below, meets no route
residuals.words: `legion gh`'s refusal of a write whose repository GitHub answers 404 to the leak guard's read of its visibility, exit 2 before gh runs (main's since #4551, leakguard's `NotFound`). A write naming another repository of the world's owner passes the world's owner refusal, meets no route and is answered `unrouted`, `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)` and exit 1. A run that makes one is unhealthy (`rig.sh health`'s rule 20, `unmodelled write`), and the run is replaced. No other write meets the refusal: the world's own repository exists, a write naming another owner is refused exit 2 before any route reads it, and the world's repository is no fork.
residuals.source: packages/pi-envoy/scripts/README.md, "Which of the world's answers are pinned, and to what"; health.ts's rule 20

residuals.name: the pull request's test merge of a head that does not merge into its base
residuals.check: stand-ins: a behaviour a stand-in declares not modelled
residuals.at: gh-standin\.ts:\d+ The test merge of a head that does not merge into its base is not modelled:
residuals.ruled: the implementer at 2026-11-21T09:31:11Z, on Main's instruction after the force-push read below; the architect may overrule it
residuals.words: GitHub's test merge (`refs/pull/<n>/merge`) of a head that does not merge into its base. GitHub keeps the last one it made: `gh api -i repos/cybermonklabs/legion/git/ref/pull/4532/merge` answered 200 at 815c2362 (Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:45:31 GMT) while the read of `pulls/4532` in the same command answered `merge_commit_sha` null; GitHub lists the pull refs after the branches (`git/refs?per_page=100&page=29`, read at 2026-11-21T08:40:07Z). The world answers none. The base never moves, but the world's remote takes a force-push of another history to the issue branch: on a copy of run 94caf2e09844's remote, `git push --force <remote> orphan:refs/heads/legion/WID-1` answered `+ a8dfa29...3b7b9ed orphan -> legion/WID-1 (forced update)`, exit 0, and `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the base and it answered `fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories`, exit 128. A run whose push leaves a head without the base's tip in its history is unhealthy from that push on (`rig.sh health`'s rule 24, `unmerged head`), and the run is replaced.
residuals.source: packages/pi-envoy/scripts/README.md, "Which of the world's answers are pinned, and to what"; health.ts's rule 24

residuals.name: a head that conflicts with its base
residuals.check: stand-ins: a behaviour a stand-in declares not modelled
residuals.at: daemon-standin\.ts:\d+ A head that conflicts with its base is not modelled,
residuals.ruled: the architect's ruling of 2026-11-21T10:17:43Z, which re-files as a residual the entry the ruling of 2026-11-19T19:03Z declared unreachable
residuals.words: A head that conflicts with its base, and everything main's daemon does about one since #4464: the second read of the same head and base a minute after a first conflicting one, the messages that ask the implementer to merge the base forward and the phase's worker to stop writing, the refusal of a completion at the head a merge forward replaced, the read of the merge state a push asks for, and the review asked once the merge lands. An agent reaches it by a forced push to the issue branch: the world's `proc-receive` hook (rig.sh's fixture_first_commit) checks no fast-forward on any branch but the base. On a scratch copy of run 94caf2e09844's remote, `git push --force <remote> orphan:refs/heads/legion/WID-1` answered `+ a8dfa29...3b7b9ed orphan -> legion/WID-1 (forced update)`, exit 0, and `git merge-tree --write-tree` of the base and that head then refused, `fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories`, exit 128. The world still reports such a head's merge state as `CLEAN` or `BLOCKED` (gh-call.ts's mergeStateOn, gh-threads.ts's mergeStateOf), and the daemon stand-in moves on no conflict. A run whose push leaves a head without the base's tip in its history is unhealthy from that push on (`rig.sh health`'s rule 24, `unmergedHead`, which names the first push to the issue branch whose head does not hold the base's tip), and the run is replaced.
residuals.source: packages/pi-envoy/scripts/README.md, "Which of the world's answers are pinned, and to what"; health.ts's rule 24
